With 8 outs though, maybe the draw is strong enough to justify the aggression. I should note this postflop tendency shift and also add that villain limped K8 from the small blind to my range data.

Hand 30: Villain SB limped Td8h. Board 9c 8s 5s 7c. Villain led flop+turn with middle pair + OESD. Hero folded.
Hand 34: Villain SB limped Js5s. Board 7d 4s 5c. Villain led flop with middle pair. Hero folded K9o.

Hand 44: Villain SB called 6cQc. Board Jd 9h 7s. Villain bet 3 with OESD (8 outs) + Qc gutshot + backdoor flush. Hero folded middle pair.
Hand 46: Villain SB called 9dJs. Board 8d Ks 6c. Villain bet 3 with OESD (T or 7 = 8 outs) + backdoor diamonds. Hero folded 2s7c.
Hand 48: Villain SB limped Qd6d. Board Jh Tc Ah. Villain bet 3 with OESD (K or 9 = 8 outs). Hero folded K-high.
Hand 50: Villain SB limped Qs5h. Board 8s Js Kh. Villain bet 3 with FLUSH DRAW (9 outs). Hero folded Ah4d.
Hand 52: Villain SB called 9s4c. Board Tc 8h 7c. Villain bet 3 with FLOPPED STRAIGHT (made nut hand). Turn 6s: hero bet 7, villain RAISED 25 with made straight. River Ks: villain bet 45 for value. Hero folded -30.
Hand 54: Villain SB limped 9cTh. Board Kd Kc 5h (DRY). Hero checked, villain bet 3 with PURE AIR (T-high, no draw). Hero folded.
Hand 56: Villain SB limped Tc8d. Board Jd 5d 6c (WET). Hero checked, villain bet 3 with GUTSHOT + backdoor flush draw. Hero folded bottom pair.

Count: 10 times villain led/bet postflop.
- Made hands: 3/10 (H30 middle pair, H34 middle pair, H52 nut straight)
- Strong draws (~6+ outs): 6/10 (H42 double gutshot, H44 OESD, H46 OESD, H48 OESD, H50 flush draw, H56 gutshot+backdoor flush)
- Pure bluff / air: 1/10 (H54 T-high on dry paired board)

REVISED PATTERN: Villain bets postflop with:
1. Made hands (value bet)
2. Strong draws on WET/CONNECTED boards (semi-bluff)
3. Air / pure bluffs on DRY boards — BOARD TEXTURE matters!

IMPLICATION: On dry boards (paired, rainbow, disconnected), villain may be bluffing. Hero can consider a call or float with showdown value. On wet/connected boards, villain likely has a hand or strong draw.
No sizing tell — small bets used across all categories.

content.thinking:
Hand 76: Villain SB limps 5cJc. Board 6s7d8s. Hero checks, villain bets 3, hero folds QsJh.

Villain's 5cJc on 6s7d8s: has a gutshot (4-5-6-7-8 = straight with a 4, or 5-6-7-8-9 = needs a 9). Actually 5-6-7-8 is there, so villain has a gutshot to a straight with a 9. This is a semi-bluff with a gutshot draw (4 outs). 

The villain also has a backdoor flush possibility with two clubs, making this more of a weak semi-bluff or near-bluff. I'm categorizing it as a pure bluff with minimal equity since the gutshot only gives 4 outs, below the 6+ threshold for strong draws. This brings my running count to 16 total hands: 3 made hands, 7 strong draws, and now 6 weak draws and bluffs with this addition.

Hero's fold with QsJh on 6s7d8s is interesting—they have queen-high with an open-ended straight draw. Looking at each possible straight: 4-5-6-7-8 and 5-6-7-8-9 don't work since hero doesn't have those cards, 6-7-8-9-T needs both 9 and T which hero doesn't have, and 7-8-9-T-J needs 9 and T as well—so that's runner-runner, not a real draw. The 8-9-T-J-Q straight also requires both 9 and T from the deck. So QJ on this 678 board actually has no straight draw at all, just queen-high, which makes folding pretty reasonable.

But wait—looking at the pot situation, villain bet 3 into about 4, and hero has two overcards to go with that queen-high. Against a range that's mostly bluffs, calling might actually be better than folding given the odds. I'm going to note this hand and add it to my villain postflop betting tracker. The count is now at 16 total bets: 3 made hands (19%), 7 strong draws with 6+ outs (44%).

The weak draws and bluffs make up the remaining 6 hands, bringing the total bluff and semibluff percentage to 81%. Now I need to update the nodes with this information.
